a combination of molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) saturation transfer difference (STD) experiments, and physicochemical analysis allows us to determine binding epitope and affinity of an antibody (Ab) for a representative set (including internal and terminal epitopes) of synthetic oligosacchride fragments of the cognate polysacchride antigen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general methodology to investigate Ab:saccharide complexes and to determine the binding mode of the Ab to the saccharide.
the development of methods that may be useful for the design of novel ligands and/or receptors, as well as for the study of carbohydrate-protein interactions.
the development of methods to characterize Ab:carbohydrate complexes, which may contribute to the design of novel vaccines or immunotherapeutics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methods described herein are useful to study carbohydrate binding and to design new synthetic oligosac-charides with improved properties.

the combination of molecular modeling and nuclear magnetic resonance experiments is a very powerful tool to characterize Ab:carbohydrate interactions, and that this strategy can be extended to the analysis of any other Ab:carbohydrates complexes.

molecular dynamics simulations and NMR saturation transfer difference experiments provide a powerful and complementary combination of methods to determine the binding mode and the binding epitope of carbohydrate antigens, even if their conformational flexibility cannot be neglected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a combination of computational and nuclear magnetic resonance techniques can be used to explore the binding epitope(s) of a carbohydrate antigen and its various contributions, as well as the ligand flexibility in an Ab:carbohydrate complex.
the dynamic aspects of carbohydrate binding to Ab may be explored using molecular dynamics simulations, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and physicochemical analysis.

the combination of computational and NMR methods allows us to characterize the binding epitope, the flexibility of ligand in the complex and the binding affinity of a representative set of oligosaccharids, without the need of using any modified oligomers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

molecular dynamics simulations and NMR spectroscopy, in combination with physicochemical analysis and molecular modeling, can be used to explore the conformational flexibility of carbohydrate ligands and their complexes with receptors, and to provide information about the binding epitopes and their contributions to affinity.

the combination of MD and STD NMR experiments, supported by physical-chemical analysis, allows one to determine the binding mode and the various contributions to affinity of a carbohydrate in a complex without using any modified ligand.

molecular modeling and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy can be combined to determine the epitope and the affinity of an antibody:oligosacharide complex, even in the absence of any modified oligosacharide.
